properties.name: 13th Apostle
properties.description: An offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: A-Frame
properties.description: The site is reasonably easily accessible and is one of the most popular shore dives.

properties.name: MV Afrikaner
properties.description: MV Afrikaner ran aground on Whale Rock in October 1993 in good weather.

properties.name: Albatross Rock
properties.description: This is a site that was mostly dived in the past on searches for wrecks of ships known to have sunk in the area after striking the reef.

properties.name: Andre se Gat
properties.description: A shoreline rocky reef.

properties.name: Ankers
properties.description: Ankers is partly sheltered from south westerly swell, and the entry area is more sheltered.

properties.name: Alpha Reef
properties.description: This is a compact reef of medium depth, and a pleasant dive.

properties.name: Ammunition Barges
properties.description: This is a shallow site and the wrecks have partly collapsed but there is still recognisable structure.

properties.name: Antipolis
properties.description: The tankers Romelia and Antipolis were under tow from Greece to scrap merchants in the Far East by the tug Kiyo Maru no.2.

properties.name: Anvil Rock 3 m Pinnacle
properties.description: The nominal position and main pinnacle at the site.

properties.name: Anvil Rock Caves
properties.description: A deeper group of pinnacles about 13 m on top lies a bit further south, where the bottom is a bit deeper than 21 m.

properties.name: MV Aster
properties.description: The wreck's position is well protected from the south easterly wind, and the depth is conveniently suitable for advanced divers.

properties.name: RMS Athens
properties.description: The "Royal Mail Ship Athens" was an iron steam screw barque of 739 tons, built in 1856 by Denny of Dumbarton and operated by the Union shipping company.

properties.name: Atlantis Reef
properties.description: Atlantis reef is a section of the granite reef of the Castle Rocks restricted zone near Partridge Point, so the marine life has been protected for many years and is flourishing.

properties.name: Bakoven Rock
properties.description: An inshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Balcony
properties.description: This site is mostly used as a training site or when conditions are marginal.

properties.name: Bantry Bay
properties.description: This little cove is at the southern end of Sea Point, towards Clifton.

properties.name: Bantry Bay Pinnacles
properties.description: A cluster of shallow pinnacles on a flattish rocky base at about 15 m These sites are in the Table Mountain National Park Marine Protected Area since 2004.

properties.name: HNMS Bato
properties.description: "His Netherlands Majesty's Ship Bato" was a Dutch warship of 800 tons and 74 guns, originally named Staaten Generaal, built in Rotterdam in 1783.

properties.name: Banging Rocks Reef
properties.description: Granite corestone reef, depth 6 m on top of the pinnacle, 19 m on sand patch a few metres to the east.

properties.name: Batsata Blinder
properties.description: The half-tide rock north of the exposed rock.

properties.name: Batsata Rock
properties.description: The rock is visible above the water at all states of the tide.

properties.name: Smiley's Reef
properties.description: A shallow (6 m) area to the west of the exposed rocks.

properties.name: Bellows Rock
properties.description: Bellows Rock is a huge granite outcrop with a relatively shallow, flattish top, with a small peak that extends above the water, and where there is almost always a strong break.

properties.name: Lusi Pinnacle
properties.description: Close by to the east of the boilers there is a rock pinnacle with its top at about 26 m with some engine structure leaning against the western side, and a fairly low ridge extends south of this.

properties.name: Lusitania Ridge pinnacle
properties.description: South of the Lusi pinnacle, across a small sandy gap there is a large ridge.

properties.name: Northeast pinnacle
properties.description: There is a pinnacle to the northeast that rises to about 15 m that was picked up on echo sounder but has probably never been dived.

properties.name: SS Bia
properties.description: The Swedish freighter SS Bia is one of at least three wrecks at Olifantsbospunt.

properties.name: Bikini Beach
properties.description: A popular swimming beach at Gordon’s Bay, not generally considered a dive site, but suitable for training exercises if the waves are not too big.

properties.name: Bill Liltved's Reef
properties.description: Bill Liltved's Reef is an area of reef to the northeast of Whittle Rock in the Off-Whittle Eastern Reefs area.

properties.name: Billy's Reef
properties.description: A small high profile reef with fairly impressive topography of deep gullies and wall-sided granite outcrops.

properties.name: SAS Bloemfontein
properties.description: HMSAS Bloemfontein was an Algerine-class minesweeper built for the Royal Navy in Canada during World War II.

properties.name: Blomvlei
properties.description: Blomvlei was built in 1935 for the National Trawling and Fishing Company of Cape Town by Smith's Dock Co. of Yorkshire.

properties.name: Blouklip
properties.description: This site is more protected than most in this area from the south westerly swell, and is accessible from the shore.

properties.name: Blousteen Ridge
properties.description: A shoreline rocky reef.

properties.name: Blue Flame North Pinnacles
properties.description: The larger section of high reef and nominal position for the area.

properties.name: Blue Flame South Pinnacles
properties.description: This is a small cluster of very steep granite corestone pinnacles about 3.8 km north of Whittle Rock.

properties.name: Deep End
properties.description: The old access road at the south east corner.

properties.name: Floating Jetty
properties.description: The site is diveable in all weather conditions, and provides a large range of depths, and is useful for training and familiarization with equipment and procedures.

properties.name: West End
properties.description: The shore at the west end, where there is easy access at the base of the north western pylon.

properties.name: Dive and Adventure Corner
properties.description: Via the old access road on the northwest corner.

properties.name: Boardroom Pinnacle
properties.description: This site has one of the largest swimthrough caves in the region, with a relatively large air-trap dome.

properties.name: Boat Rock
properties.description: An inshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Bordjiesrif
properties.description: A shoreline rocky reef.

properties.name: North Pinnacle
properties.description: A reef area due east of the main reef at Whittle Rock, and due south of Off-Whittle Ridge, shown on the SAN chart as a shallower area, and known by fishermen, but not known to have been dived before 2021.

properties.name: Western Pinnacle
properties.description: The 23 m pinnacle near the middle of on the western lobe.

properties.name: Caves
properties.description: A reef area due east of the main reef at Whittle Rock, and due south of Off-Whittle Ridge, shown on the SAN chart as a shallower area, and known by fishermen, but not known to have been dived before 2021.

properties.name: Bruce's Mark
properties.description: The 17 m pinnacles at the southern end of the eastern lobe.

properties.name: Brunswick
properties.description: The Brunswick was an English East Indiaman of 1 200 tons, an armed merchant ship of 30 guns that transported goods between Britain and the East Indies.

properties.name: Buffels Bay
properties.description: A shoreline rocky reef.

properties.name: Canyon
properties.description: Canyon is a relatively deep site first named in 2013, and may be diveable when the other sites nearby have too much surge.

properties.name: SS Cape Matapan
properties.description: An offshore historical wreck.

properties.name: Caravan Central East Pinnacle
properties.description: Caravan Reef is a large area of granite reef to the north east of the slipway at Miller's Point, and as such is very close to the launch area.

properties.name: Caravan Central North Pinnacle
properties.description: Caravan Reef is a large area of granite reef to the north east of the slipway at Miller's Point, and as such is very close to the launch area.

properties.name: Inner Caravan Reef
properties.description: Caravan Reef is a large area of granite reef to the north east of the slipway at Miller's Point, and as such is very close to the launch area.

properties.name: North Caravan Reef
properties.description: Caravan Reef is a large area of granite reef to the north east of the slipway at Miller's Point, and as such is very close to the launch area.

properties.name: PMB Pinnacles
properties.description: Named for its proximity to the wreck of SAS Pietermaritzburg

properties.name: South Caravan Reef
properties.description: Caravan Reef is a large area of granite reef to the north east of the slipway at Miller's Point, and as such is very close to the launch area.

properties.name: North Castle
properties.description: This area has a fairly shallow rocky bottom with granite boulders and outcrops of moderate height near the entry point.

properties.name: Castle Rocks Point Reefs
properties.description: The bottom of the deeper gullies is sand with steep sided ridges between, of varied length, width and height.

properties.name: Inner Castle
properties.description: South Side, or Inner Castle, is the sandy bay visible from the roadside to the south of the point.

properties.name: Central Pinnacle
properties.description: Castor Rock is close to the launch site at False Bay Yacht Club and the Simon's Town jetty, and is relatively sheltered from southwesterly swell.

properties.name: Northern Pinnacle
properties.description: Castor Rock is close to the launch site at False Bay Yacht Club and the Simon's Town jetty, and is relatively sheltered from southwesterly swell.

properties.name: Roman's Rest
properties.description: Drop off at the pinnacle, visit the twin pinnacles, explore the reef and ascend at the pinnacle.

properties.name: Southeast Pinnacle
properties.description: A locally shallow area on the southern part of the north lobe.

properties.name: Southwest Pinnacle
properties.description: The high point of an area of local high profile reef on the eastern edge of the north lobe.

properties.name: Wonders Pinnacle
properties.description: Drop off at the pinnacle, dive the surrounding reef and ascend at the pinnacle.

properties.name: SS Clan Monroe
properties.description: The Clan Monroe was a British turret steamer and sister ship to the SS Clan Stuart, which was wrecked on the other side of the Cape Peninsula at Simon's Town, only 11 km away as the crow flies.

properties.name: SS Clan Stuart
properties.description: The "SS Clan Stuart", a 3594 ton steel British turret steamer carrying a cargo of coal, ran aground after dragging its anchor in a southeasterly gale on 21 November 1914.

properties.name: Cleeve's Tunnel
properties.description: The site is notable for the relatively long and fairly tight swim-through tunnel under a large pinnacle.

properties.name: Clifton Rocks
properties.description: An inshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Colebrooke
properties.description: The Colebrooke was a wood ship of 739 tons built in 1770 at the Blackwall yard on the Thames, in London for the Honourable East India Company.

properties.name: Container Bay
properties.description: This is a site which you might dive if you are staying at Rooi-els or nearby, and wanted a bit of variety.

properties.name: Coral Gardens (inshore pinnacles)
properties.description: This inshore pinnacle is a group of very tall boulders out to the west of the point, with kelp on top reaching the surface at low tide.

properties.name: Coral Gardens Offshore Pinnacle
properties.description: There is a sheer sided pinnacle near the outer blinder, which extends to within about 3 m of the surface, and down to about 20 m.

properties.name: Coral Gardens
properties.description: This site has interesting and varied topography and large numbers of colourful sponges, ascidians, soft corals and sea fans.

properties.name: Cow and Calf
properties.description: The gap between high reef ridges and shore is about 5 to 8 m deep, with low ridges and boulders.

properties.name: Stone Dog
properties.description: Cow and Calf is a reasonably accessible shore dive close to Gordon's Bay, in an area relatively protected from south westerly swell, and provides a reasonable range of depth and good variety of reef life.

properties.name: MV Daeyang Family
properties.description: This is the wreck of a very large ship.

properties.name: Dale Brook
properties.description: This site is well known in the scientific literature for a large variety of species, and it has been a sanctuary zone for a long time, but is seldom dived by sport divers.

properties.name: Deep South Whittle Reef
properties.description: One of the closest 50 m+ reef dives to Simon's Town.

properties.name: D-Frame
properties.description: This is a pleasant reef, not dived very frequently.

properties.name: Die Josie
properties.description: A reef which is close to Hout Bay harbour and is suitable for night dives.

properties.name: Die Perd
properties.description: An inshore, rocky reef.

properties.name: Di's Cracks 9 m Pinnacle
properties.description: Big pointy topped boulder jammed into the top of a crack with a big swimthrough underneath.

properties.name: Di's Cracks 14 m pinnacle
properties.description: Very big flat topped pinnacle - boulder on top of main reef outcrop.

properties.name: Disa
properties.description: The Disa was built for Irvin and Johnson in 1959 in Yorkshire, England by Cook, Welton and Gemmell.

properties.name: Dome Rock
properties.description: An offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Dreadlocks Reef
properties.description: The site is colourful and fairly spectacular, and is specially notable for the relatively large colonies of the Dreadlocks hydroid Myriothela tentaculata.

properties.name: East Shoal
properties.description: The site is seldom dived, as it is far from the nearest launch sites, and relatively close to Seal Island where Great White sharks are frequently seen predating on the Cape fur seals which breed there.

properties.name: East shoal - South Pinnacle
properties.description: Low dip c5 to 10 degrees about N. Large blocky sandstone outcrop, mostly not very steep below 20m, but with quite a long wall around much of the peak at between 19 and about 7m.

properties.name: False Bay Yacht Club moorings
properties.description: This is not a popular dive site, but it is the base for the biennial Cape Town Dive Festival, and the water is suitable for testing equipment and buoyancy before a boat dive.

properties.name: Fan Reef
properties.description: The site has a large concentration of fairly large gorgonian sea fans

properties.name: Finlay's Point
properties.description: The site is sometimes used as an alternative when conditions are found to be unsuitable on the planned site further south on the peninsula, as visibility here has been considerably better on those occasions.

properties.name: Carnaby Street Pinnacle
properties.description: Large granite outcrop and large boulders on an extensive area of granite corestone reef bordered by sandy areas to the south and east, Graeme's Spot to the north, and Finlay's Pinnacle to the west.

properties.name: Finlay's Pinnacle
properties.description: Large granite outcrop and boulders on an extensive area of granite corestone reef bordered by a sandy strip to the south.

properties.name: Graeme's Spot
properties.description: The local high spot on the northern lobe of reef.

properties.name: The Jambles
properties.description: An area of high reef with gullies, cracks and crevices and large boulders with overhangs and small caves along the edge of the reef with sand at the bottom.

properties.name: Finlay's Deep
properties.description: This is a small reef with a large number of Gorgonian sea fans.

properties.name: Fisherman's Beach
properties.description: A shoreline rocky reef.

properties.name: Fish Hoek Reef
properties.description: An offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: SAS Fleur
properties.description: The "SAS Fleur" was a 'Bar' class boom defence vessel, formerly HMS Barbrake, built by William Simons and Co. in Renfrew, Scotland, and commissioned in 1942.

properties.name: Friskies Pinnacle
properties.description: Friskies and North Friskes are two of a large group of reefs scattered around the area marked by the Roman Rock lighthouse.

properties.name: North Friskies Pinnacle
properties.description: Friskies and North Friskes are two of a large group of reefs scattered around the area marked by the Roman Rock lighthouse.

properties.name: Froggy pond
properties.description: A shore dive site which is suitable for training exercises as it is sheltered and has a flat sandy bottom.

properties.name: West drop
properties.description: Nice reef, pleasant, but not very spectacular topography in the area visited.

properties.name: GB Reef
properties.description: Nice reef, pleasant, but not very spectacular topography in the area visited.

properties.name: GB South Reef
properties.description: Found during a multibeam sonar survey of False Bay by Wreckless Marine in about 2022, and first dived in October 2025 by Wreckless Divers.

properties.name: SAS Gelderland
properties.description: The "SAS Gelderland" was a Ford class Seaward Defense Boat, formerly the HMS Brayford, renamed on 30th August 1954.

properties.name: Plan B pinnacle
properties.description: A pretty reef, compact and high profile, but not very big.

properties.name: Plan C pinnacle
properties.description: Much the same dive plan applies as for Plan B, though the high reef is smaller, and there may not be wreckage.

properties.name: Geldkis Blinder
properties.description: An inshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Geldkis
properties.description: The site has rugged topography, with walls, swinthroughs, gullies, overhangs and chimneys and varied and colourful sea life, and is spectacular in good visibility.

properties.name: MV Gemsbok
properties.description: An offshore deep recent wreck.

properties.name: SATS General Botha
properties.description: This site is considered one of the more interesting wreck dives of False Bay, and the depth appeals to the more adventurous divers.

properties.name: Giant's Castle
properties.description: This is one of the deeper reef sites within a short distance from the popular False Bay launching areas.

properties.name: Glencairn Fan Garden
properties.description: This site is known for the large numbers of gorgonian sea fans in relatively shallow water

properties.name: ST Godetia
properties.description: The ST Godetia was a steel steam side-trawler in the Irvin and Johnson fleet, which was sunk by the SA Air force as target practice in August 1970.

properties.name: SAS Good Hope
properties.description: A recent wreck.

properties.name: Good Hope Reef
properties.description: This is a small granite reef on a sandy bottom with lots of gorgonian sea fans.

properties.name: Groot Pannekoek
properties.description: This was a site used for a scientific instrument station, and was regularly visited by scientific divers for instrument maintenance.

properties.name: Die Middelmas
properties.description: Die Middelmas is a rock that projects above the water at all tides, to the west of the Oude Schip peninsula.

properties.name: Peet's Pinnacle
properties.description: Peet's Pinnacle is a steep sided corestone boulder pinnacle rising from about 23 m on the sand to the west up to a reported 8 m on top, surrounded by lower reef, first reported by local diver Peet van Eeden.

properties.name: Hakka Reef Southeast Pinnacles
properties.description: Southeast Pinnacles are a pair of high pinnacles to the southeast of the exposed rock.

properties.name: Hakka Reef Sven's Caves pinnacles
properties.description: Sven's Caves is a group of deep overhangs and swimthroughs at about 20 m depth on the south side of a group of high profile pinnacles to the east of the exposed rock, first reported by local diver Sven Huckveld.

properties.name: MV Harvest Capella
properties.description: An inshore recent wreck.

properties.name: Hermes
properties.description: A shallow wreck site on a sand bottom, within swimming distance of the beach.

properties.name: Het Huis te Kraaiestein
properties.description: "Het Huis te Kraaiestein" was a Dutch ship of 1,154 tons, built in 1697 at the Zeeland Yard for the Zeeland Chamber of the Dutch East India Company, and commanded by Jan van de Vijver.

properties.name: Highfields
properties.description: The Highfields was a British four-masted steel barque commanded by Capt E.R. Dunham.

properties.name: Humpback Ridge
properties.description: A fairly massive granite pinnacle in the middle of a more extensive north-south ridge rising to about 12 m.

properties.name: SS Hypatia
properties.description: SS Hypatia was wrecked on Whale Rock in Table Bay on 29 October 1929 in fog while on a voyage from Beira to New York with a cargo of blister copper and chrome ore.

properties.name: Insanity Reef
properties.description: An offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: NE pinnacle
properties.description: Josh's Reef is a fairly large patch of granite corestone reef south of Whittle Rock reef, surrounded by sand at about 48 m, rising to 32 m on top, with nice ledges to the southwest with a fine display of noble corals.

properties.name: Central pinnacle
properties.description: Josh's Reef is a fairly large patch of granite corestone reef south of Whittle Rock reef, surrounded by sand at about 48 m, rising to 32 m on top, with nice ledges to the southwest with a fine display of noble corals.

properties.name: Noble pinnacle
properties.description: To the southwest of the shallowest area there is a relatively high profile area known as Noble Point, for the fine display of noble corals seen there.

properties.name: SW pinnacle
properties.description: Josh's Reef is a fairly large patch of granite corestone reef south of Whittle Rock reef, surrounded by sand at about 48 m, rising to 32 m on top, with nice ledges to the southwest with a fine display of noble corals.

properties.name: South pinnacle
properties.description: Josh's Reef is a fairly large patch of granite corestone reef south of Whittle Rock reef, surrounded by sand at about 48 m, rising to 32 m on top, with nice ledges to the southwest with a fine display of noble corals.

properties.name: Justin's Caves
properties.description: The site has spectacular topography and colourful ecology, and is justly one of the more popular shore dives of Cape Town.

properties.name: Kalk Bay Harbour Wall
properties.description: The herbour wall site is mostly used for commercial diver training and collecting lead sinkers and other fishing gear lost from the harbour wall.

properties.name: Kanobi's Wall
properties.description: This is a good site for rugged topography, biodiversity and depth range.

properties.name: MV Katsu Maru
properties.description: On the evening of 8th July 1978, the Japanese trawler Katsu Maru #25 was sailing in thick fog 22 nm West of Slangkop Lighthouse, when it was in collision with the 18,600 ton Norwegian tanker Team Pollux .

properties.name: MV Ker Yar Vor and the Jo May
properties.page: MV Ker Yar Vor and the Jo May
properties.description: The Ker Yar Vor was a 292 ton steel lobster fishing vessel built in Ostende, Belgium, and registered in Cape Town which was sunk on 10th August 1979 in Maori Bay.

properties.name: King Emperor
properties.description: The site is the wreck of a steel steam trawler in reasonably good structural condition.

properties.name: Klein Pannekoek
properties.description: An inshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Klein Tafelberg Reef
properties.description: This can be a spectacular dive in good visibility as the reef profile is very rugged.

properties.name: Kruis
properties.description: A shoreline rocky reef.

properties.name: Ledges
properties.description: A shoreline rocky reef.

properties.name: Livingstone Reef
properties.description: Fairly high profile corestone reef around the pinnacle, and another large outcrop some way to the east.

properties.name: Logies Bay
properties.description: This site is the small cove to the north of Llandudno beach.

properties.name: Lonehill Reef
properties.description: An offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Long Beach
properties.description: At first glance the site seems bland, but careful investigation will reveal interesting and varied life.

properties.name: Lorry Bay
properties.description: The site is partly enclosed and often used for training and night dives.

properties.name: SS Lusitania
properties.description: The SS Lusitania was a Portuguese twin-screw liner of 5557 tons, built in 1906 by Sir Raylton Dixon & Co, and owned by Empreza Nacional De Navegacao, of Lisbon.

properties.name: Ammo Reef
properties.description: To the east of Maidstone reef, is a fairly monolithic outcrop with a marked groove along the length of top, and parallel jointing to the north east.

properties.name: Anchor Reef, or Maidstone Reef
properties.description: Anchor Reef, or Maidstone Reef, is a large, fairly flat topped area of bedrock that extends a few metres above the sand.

properties.name: Maidstone Rock
properties.description: This is the highest of a cluster of very precipitous granite pinnacles on fairly flat sand bottom.

properties.name: SS Maori
properties.description: This is one of the most popular wreck dives of this region, as it is of historical interest, in good condition for its age, reasonably sheltered and fairly shallow.

properties.name: Midway Ridge
properties.description: Found during a multibeam sonar survey and first dived in October 2022 by Wreckless Divers.

properties.name: Mike's Point
properties.description: An inshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Rumbly Bay
properties.description: This small beach is on the South side of Miller’s Point, facing Rumbly Bay, and with Castle Rocks in the background.

properties.name: Miller's Point slipway
properties.description: The Miller's Point slipway is in the nortwest of the point, where the coastline extends to the north.

properties.name: Miller's Point tidal pool
properties.description: There is a small beach and a small protected inlet at the tip of the point at S34°13.934’ E018°28.577’.

properties.name: Moddergat
properties.description: This is a dive site which is close to the slipway at Harbour Island, and deep enough that the visibility at the bottom may be significantly better than in the shallower water of the shoreline dive sites of Gordon's Bay.

properties.name: Mooivlei
properties.description: The site is at the wreck of a steam powered steel side trawler, scuttled at the end of its useful service life.

properties.name: Murphy's
properties.description: This is an alternative site in the Millers Point area, just outside the Castle Rocks restricted zone of the Marine Protected Area

properties.name: ST Bulby, or Eastern trawler wreck
properties.description: Limited access to the hull of the eastern wreck is possible through the deck frames, as the decking is gone.

properties.name: ST Borella
properties.description: The wreck lies on sand at 18 m, aligned roughly northeast-southwest between the Bulby and the Iolite, with the bow to the southwest, and tilted to port, with the whole port side buried in the sand.

properties.name: ST Iolite or Western trawler wreck
properties.description: This is a dive site which is seldom visited, and is visited mainly as a change from the more popular sites by local divers who have seen most of the other wrecks in the region and feel like a change.

properties.name: Mushroom Pinnacle
properties.description: The pinnacle is a submerged granite tor (stacked group of large corestones) between Geldkis and Justin’s Caves.

properties.name: Noah's Ark Rock
properties.description: This is a huge flat topped granite boulder standing on even larger granite outcrop which extends above the sand level.

properties.name: Ark Rock Barge wreck
properties.description: This wreck comprises the central section of a steel barge, probably a dredging hopper.

properties.name: Ark Rock Boiler wreck #1
properties.description: This wreck is the remains of a small unidentified iron or steel vessel which has mostly rusted away, except for the boiler, what might be the engine crankcase and some of the nearby structure.

properties.name: Ark Rock Boiler wreck #2
properties.description: This wreck is the remains of a small steam powered wooden vessel.

properties.name: Ark Rock Boiler wreck #3b
properties.description: All that is visible of this wreck are two boilers.

properties.name: Parana wreck, small section
properties.description: The wreckage of an iron or steel ship which may be the Parana.

properties.name: Noah's Ark - Double row of concrete pillars
properties.description: These are minor wrecks of some historical interest and a large exposed rock surrounded by a small high profile reef.

properties.name: Noah's Ark - Single row of concrete pillars
properties.description: There are two groups of concrete pillars aligned in rows on the sand bottom.

properties.name: Noah's Ark - Eastern wreck
properties.description: To the east of Ark Rock is a small iron or steel wreck.

properties.name: Noah's Ark - Heat exchanger
properties.description: A heavily overgrown piece of wreckage about 2 m long and 1.5 m diameter lies on a fairly extensive and moderately flat rubble bottom at about 9 m depth.

properties.name: Noah's Ark - Twin barges
properties.description: Two small steel barges, each about 17 m long and 4 m wide, in reasonably intact condition about 320 m north of Ark Rock, lying on sand at 23 m.

properties.name: North Island Reef
properties.description: The reef was found during a multibeam sonar survey of False Bay by Wreckless Marine in about 2022, and first dived in October 2026 by Wreckless Divers.

properties.name: Barry's Pinnacles
properties.description: The two lesser pinnacles to the east reach up to about 20 m.

properties.name: Cave Rock
properties.description: About 75 m to the west of the exposed rocks.

properties.name: Eastern Pinnacle
properties.description: The Eastern Pinnacle is about 45 m wide east to west and 40 m north to south at the 18 m contour.

properties.name: Main Reef
properties.description: The main reef is a cluster of huge granite corestone boulders, on a base of low granite reef.

properties.name: Monty's Pinnacles
properties.description: This can be a spectacular site in good conditions.

properties.name: Northern Pinnacles
properties.description: Extensive areas to the north are about 21 m or slightly less.

properties.name: SS Oakburn and MV Bos 400
properties.description: The site is mainly interesting for the wreck of the BOS 400, and what remains of the Oakburn.

properties.name: North Barge
properties.description: This is one of the closest 40 m wreck dives to a convenient launch site in False Bay

properties.name: South Barge
properties.description: This is one of the closest 40 m wreck dives to a convenient launch site in False Bay

properties.name: Off-Whittle Ridge
properties.description: Off-Whittle Ridge is an area of reef to the northwest of Whittle Rock.

properties.name: Bruce's drop
properties.description: The invertebrate cover is diverse, particularly the sponges.

properties.name: Omega North pinnacle
properties.description: Shallowest point and usual drop point.

properties.name: Omega Northwest Pinnacle
properties.description: Part of the lower reef section slightly up the slope of the sand to the northwest.

properties.name: Omega Central pinnacle
properties.description: High point on the main outcrop.There is a second, slightly deeper shallow area about halfway along the reef toward the south-east, which rises to about 15 m,with a large area above 18 m.

properties.name: MFV Orotava
properties.description: Like the other wrecks of Smitswinkel Bay, the MV Orotava is reasonably accessible and a popular dive site for both local and visiting divers.

properties.name: Outer Photographer's Reef
properties.description: An offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: P87 wreck
properties.description: Wreckage of a small wooden naval patrol boat on a sand bottom.

properties.name: Big Rock
properties.description: This site is in the vicinity of the highest rock in the area.

properties.name: Big swim-through
properties.description: Fish, seals and a wide range of invertebrates can be seen in surroundings which can be spectacular in good conditions.

properties.name: Dave's Caves
properties.description: Fish, seals and a wide range of invertebrates can be seen in surroundings which can be spectacular in good conditions.

properties.name: Deep Partridge
properties.description: The eastern edge of the reef is at about 25 m on fine sand.

properties.name: Fish Tank
properties.description: Fish tank is a small section of reef to the north of Seal Rock across about 50 m of sand.

properties.name: Joe's Spot
properties.description: An area near the north edge of the Seal Rock lobe, northeast of the exposed rock, enclosed on three sides by high reef with deep gullies between.

properties.name: Partridge Central
properties.description: Beyond the sandy patch to the north of the Big Rock is more moderate profile reef, partly mapped.

properties.name: Peter's Pinnacles
properties.description: The main pinnacle to the south west of the site is a granite tor extending to within about 4 m of the surface at low tide, and about 30 m wide from east to west at the base.

properties.name: Seal Rock
properties.description: Fish, seals and a wide range of invertebrates can be seen in surroundings which can be spectacular in good conditions.

properties.name: Penguin Point
properties.description: This is a shallow dive site with easy access and good facilities.

properties.name: Percy's Hole
properties.description: This is one of the best known and most interesting sites on the east side of False Bay.

properties.name: Phil's Bay
properties.description: A shoreline rocky reef.

properties.name: SAS Pietermaritzburg
properties.description: The keel of this Algerine class ocean minesweeper was laid down on 8th October 1942 at Lobnitz and Co. Renfrewshire, the ship was launched on 18th June 1943 and completed on 7th October 1943.

properties.name: Pinnacle
properties.description: This site has very varied topography, which provides a large range of habitats, and these provide shelter for a large diversity of organisms.

properties.name: Phoenix shoal
properties.description: The Phoenix was a British ship of 500 tons, built in 1810.

properties.name: Photographer's Reef
properties.description: An inshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Phone Reef
properties.description: This site is moderately deep, but shallow enough for a fairly long dive on nitrox.

properties.name: East Pie Rock Reef
properties.page: Pie Rock and Outer Castle reefs
properties.description: Top at 12 m, a small cluster of tall pinnacles with deep cracks between them, with sand edge nearby to the northeast at about 24 to 24 m.

properties.name: North Pie Rock
properties.page: Pie Rock and Outer Castle reefs
properties.description: Pie Rock North Pinnacles is two adjacent groups of high pinnacles south of the Outer Castle blinder.

properties.name: Outer Castle
properties.page: Pie Rock and Outer Castle reefs
properties.description: The main feature of the section is a huge granite boulder on a rock base standing on four points with a swim-through gap underneath.

properties.name: South Pie Rock Pinnacles
properties.page: Pie Rock and Outer Castle reefs
properties.description: Pie Rock Southern Pinnacles are part of a more extensive area of low reef to the south, with a picturesque group of shallow pinnacles rising to about 4 m depth at the shallowest point, and a fairly large area above 15 m.

properties.name: West Pie Rock Reef
properties.page: Pie Rock and Outer Castle reefs
properties.description: Pie Rock West Reef is a relatively shallow area west of the north and south pinnacles, with a shallow point at about 4 m depth, a large area above 12 m, and almost all the rest above 15 m.

properties.name: MFV Princess Elizabeth
properties.description: This is one of the best preserved of the Cape Town wrecks.

properties.name: Castle Pinnacles
properties.page: Pyramid Rock reef and Shark Alley
properties.description: A group of fairly tall pinnacles along the edge of the sand.

properties.name: Pyramid Reef East Pinnacle
properties.page: Pyramid Rock reef and Shark Alley
properties.description: A shallow area of small pinnacles northeast of Pyramid Rock.

properties.name: Pyramid Rock
properties.page: Pyramid Rock reef and Shark Alley
properties.description: Between Miller’s Point and Castle Rocks, a short distance offshore (about 250 m).

properties.name: Sansui Reef
properties.page: Pyramid Rock reef and Shark Alley
properties.description: An area of small ridges and boulders on a rippled white sand bottom near the Castle Pinnacles.

properties.name: Shark Alley
properties.page: Pyramid Rock reef and Shark Alley
properties.description: A mostly sandy bottomed site between Pyramid Reef and the shoreline reef between Rumbly Bay and Castle Rock.

properties.name: Quarry
properties.description: An inshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Quarry Barge
properties.description: An offshore recent wreck on a rocky reef.

properties.name: Rachel's Reef
properties.description: This is a pleasant little pinnacle with extensive deeper surrounding reef.

properties.name: Hotlips Pinnacle
properties.description: The reef is a compact granite outcrop, surrounded by sand, rising to about 18 m on top, and running roughly east to west.

properties.name: Rambler Rock North-central Reef
properties.description: Quite a large section of reef approximately central between North-west pinnacle and North-east reefs.

properties.name: Rambler Rock Northeast Reefs
properties.description: Extensive fairly low profile reef with areas of moderately high profile boulders.

properties.name: Rambler Rock Northwest Pinnacle
properties.description: A pinnacle of very large boulders and outcrops concentrated in an area about 25 m diameter.

properties.name: Rambler Rock Southern pinnacles
properties.description: Extensive granite reef.

properties.name: Reef With No Name (little pinnacles)
properties.description: A patch of offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Rudy's Random Rocks
properties.description: A patch of offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Reigersdaal
properties.description: On 25 October 1747, the Dutch East Indiaman Reigersdaal was wrecked at Silwerstroomstrand.

properties.name: Robben Island steamer wreck Gilia
properties.description: The wreck is not marked on the navigational charts, and there is no known record of a wreck at this position, but there are many wrecks in Table Bay for which the position is not accurately recorded.

properties.name: MV Rockeater
properties.description: The Rockeater is a relatively bulky wreck for its length compared with the frigates Good Hope and Transvaal, and is quite a bit larger than the fishing boats Orotava and Princess Elizabeth.

properties.name: Rocklands Blinder
properties.description: An inshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Buttress
properties.description: A magnificent buttress about 45 m on top dropping off steeply to 60 m.

properties.name: Wreckless Rock
properties.description: This site has a different ambience to other Cape Peninsula and False Bay sites, and may have better visibility much of the time.

properties.name: Mossie se Rif
properties.description: This site has a different ambience to other Cape Peninsula and False Bay sites, and may have better visibility much of the time.

properties.name: East Pinnacle
properties.description: This site has a different ambience to other Cape Peninsula and False Bay sites, and may have better visibility much of the time.

properties.name: The Rock
properties.description: An area of unusually high profile blocky reef with depths between about 33 and 45 m.

properties.name: Gully
properties.description: A long shallow east-west depression that runs across the bank with a minimum depth of about 32 m in the middle, with slightly shallower low profile reef to the north and south.

properties.name: Shoal Point
properties.description: The shallowest part of the reef as surveyed.

properties.name: Duke's Ridge
properties.description: This site has a different ambience to other Cape Peninsula and False Bay sites, and may have better visibility much of the time.

properties.name: Rocky Ridge North
properties.description: This site has a different ambience to other Cape Peninsula and False Bay sites, and may have better visibility much of the time.

properties.name: Rocky Ridge
properties.description: A long east–west gnarly drop-off about 5 to 8 m high, with heavy encrustation of noble corals and sponges on the wall.

properties.name: Rocky Ridge South
properties.description: This site has a different ambience to other Cape Peninsula and False Bay sites, and may have better visibility much of the time.

properties.name: Pablo's Steps
properties.description: Drop onto about 36m and travel northwest up a series of low steps.

properties.name: Ahmed's Bluff
properties.description: A low bluff structure at about 45 m, dropping off to about 50 m.

properties.name: The Corner
properties.description: This site has a different ambience to other Cape Peninsula and False Bay sites, and may have better visibility much of the time.

properties.name: Deep Ridge
properties.description: Other marks have also been used before the reef was surveyed in high resolution.

properties.name: Rocky Bay
properties.description: An inshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Noble Reef
properties.description: Usually a boat dive as finding it from a shore entry is largely a matter of luck without a GPS.

properties.name: Roman Rock
properties.description: An easy dive site to find as it is marked by the lighthouse of the same name off Simon’s Town Harbour.

properties.name: Roman Rock North
properties.description: A fairly large but relatively low expanse of reef roughly northwest of the lighthouse, of no known special interest.

properties.name: Roman Rock South
properties.description: There is a smaller section of reef to the south across a small belt of sand roughly parallel to Roman Rock main reef.

properties.name: Spider Crab Reefs
properties.description: Two small parallel reefs to the west of Roman Rock, rising from sand at about 21 m to 16 m at the shallowest point.

properties.name: MV Romelia
properties.description: The tankers MV Romelia and MV Antipolis were under tow by the tug Kiyo Maru no.2 from Greece to scrap merchants in the Far East.

properties.name: Rooi-els Point
properties.description: The point at Rooi-els seems an obvious place for a dive site.

properties.name: Sandy Cove
properties.description: The site is popular for open water training exercises, refresher courses and testing equipment when you don’t need depth.

properties.name: Sandy-top Ridge
properties.description: A smallish granite outcrop rising from about 48 m on the sand to about 32 m deep at the flattish top, which has a sandy depression roughly central on the high reef.

properties.name: São José Paquete d' Africa
properties.description: The São José Paquete d' Africa is the wreck of a Portuguese slave ship of historical and cultural interest, but there is little wreckage remaining.

properties.name: SS SA Seafarer
properties.description: The Safmarine freighter SS South African Seafarer was wrecked in a north westerly gale on 1st July, 1966, in front of the Green Point Lighthouse.

properties.name: Duiker Island
properties.description: This is a site where you will see Cape fur seals, close up and in your face, both in the water and on the rocks.

properties.name: Seal Island
properties.description: Seal Island is the only true island in False Bay.

properties.name: Sea Point Ridge Pinnacles
properties.description: The site is conveniently close to the slipway at Oceana Power Boat Club in Granger Bay, and is shallow enough for advanced recreational divers.

properties.name: MV Seli 1
properties.description: Seli 1 was a bilk carrier of 18534 tons, built by Hyundai Heavy Industries, and originally named Asia Sun.

properties.name: Sentinel
properties.description: This is the place on the Atlantic seaboard where the 30 m contour is closest to the shore

properties.name: Sherwood Forest
properties.description: The site has exceptional sea fans.

properties.name: Sickle Reef
properties.description: One of the smaller and lower profile reefs in this sector, but has a lot of biodiversity, possibly due to relatively high rugosity.

properties.name: Simon's Town Jetty
properties.description: This is not a popular dive site, but it is a popular loading and unloading area for dive charters, and the water is suitable for testing equipment and buoyancy before a boat dive.

properties.name: Smits Cliff
properties.description: The site is not dived very often as there are more popular sites which are more accessible.

properties.name: Batsata Maze
properties.description: Batsata Maze is a small section of the reef towards the southeast where a jumble of large boulders lie on top of the lower outcrops and form a group of swim-throughs, overhangs, gaps and caves.

properties.name: Horseshoe Reef
properties.description: Horseshoe Reef is the northeastern section, comprising the northern ridge and the east face of the main reef.

properties.name: Kreef Reef
properties.description: Kreef Reef is a large, relatively low, outlier to the north west of Smits Reef.

properties.name: Smits Reef
properties.description: The south west corner of the main reef also has some pretty rugged profile, and the big overhang on the 15 m contour is worth a visit.

properties.name: Western Pinnacle
properties.description: The West Reef is across a sandy bottomed gap from the west side of the main reef.

properties.name: South Island Reef
properties.description: This site was found during a multibeam sonar survey of False Bay by Wreckless Marine in 2022, and first dived in September 2025 by Wreckless Divers.

properties.name: North pinnacle
properties.description: This reef was marked on the SAN chart as a spot depth and ring contour indicating a small area shallower than 50 m, and identified as a small, isolated, rocky reef during a multibeam sonar survey of False Bay.

properties.name: Central
properties.description: This is near the northwest end of the highest ridge, which slopes down quite steeply to the sand to the southwest, and at the southeastern end of a shallow gully in the ridge which extends northwest and deeper.

properties.name: Spaniard Rock
properties.description: An inshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Star of Africa
properties.description: An offshore rocky reef with a historical wreck.

properties.name: Star Walls Pinnacle
properties.description: Shallowest point on top of the main outcrop at Star Walls.

properties.name: M&M Cave
properties.description: Somewhat to the north east of the wall, at S34°02.409' E018°18.189', the M&M pinnacles rise from the edge of the eastern sand patch at roughly 24m depth to about 10m on top.

properties.name: Lollipop Pinnacle
properties.description: About 150 m to the south east of Star Wall, at the edge of the southern sand patch, and about half way to Sunfish pinnacle, is a monolithic boulder resting on top of the bedrock reef at about 25 m depth.

properties.name: Choirboys Reef
properties.description: This region is a long ridge running approximately north-south, about two thirds of the way across False Bay from the Cape Peninsula.

properties.name: Drop Zone (north)
properties.description: The name "Drop Zone" was given to the site by Indigo Divers of Gordons Bay.

properties.name: Drop Zone (south)
properties.description: This region is a long ridge running approximately north-south, about two thirds of the way across False Bay from the Cape Peninsula.

properties.name: Mossie's Reef
properties.description: This region is a long ridge running approximately north-south, about two thirds of the way across False Bay from the Cape Peninsula.

properties.name: Mossie's Reef South
properties.description: This region is a long ridge running approximately north-south, about two thirds of the way across False Bay from the Cape Peninsula.

properties.name: Snake Ridge
properties.description: Part of the sedimentary rock outcrop, south of Steenbras Deep, which has a ridge top running approximately north-south.

properties.name: Steenbras Deep North Pinnacle or 2nd Pinnacle
properties.description: Irregular shaped reef about 40 m diameter at 21 m, of hard, fine-grained sedimentary rock.

properties.name: Steenbras Deep South Pinnacle or 1st Pinnacle
properties.description: Large area of irregular shape, about 130 m east to west and 200 m north to south at 27 m, with the top at about 19 m.

properties.name: Steenbras Koppie
properties.description: A small close cluster of steep sided high profile outcrops with shelly sand between them.

properties.name: Steenbras Ridge Edge
properties.description: This region is a long ridge running approximately north-south, about two thirds of the way across False Bay from the Cape Peninsula.

properties.name: Steenbras Ridge Outpost
properties.description: A small outlier to the east of the ridge, comprising a small area of jagged edged outcrop with steep dip, rising a few metres above a larger are of low reef of rubble, mostly in the sub-metre size range.

properties.name: Steenbras Ridge River Mouth Pinnacle
properties.description: Steenbras Ridge River Mouth Pinnacle, also known as Steenbras Deep Far North.

properties.name: Sterretjies Reef
properties.description: The area is indicated on the SAN chart as a shoal area above 20 m, with a spot depth of 15 m.

properties.name: Whale Reef
properties.description: This region is a long ridge running approximately north-south, about two thirds of the way across False Bay from the Cape Peninsula.

properties.name: No. 11 reef
properties.description: This region is a long ridge running approximately north-south, about two thirds of the way across False Bay from the Cape Peninsula.

properties.name: No. 12 reef
properties.description: This region is a long ridge running approximately north-south, about two thirds of the way across False Bay from the Cape Peninsula.

properties.name: No. 8 reef
properties.description: This region is a long ridge running approximately north-south, about two thirds of the way across False Bay from the Cape Peninsula.

properties.name: Inner ridge north
properties.description: This region is a long ridge running approximately north-south, about two thirds of the way across False Bay from the Cape Peninsula.

properties.name: Stef's Reef
properties.description: The main reef area is to the north, with the high section at the south end, near the sandy gully.

properties.name: Stef's Reef Ridge
properties.description: The southern part of the reef is distinguished by a long, high, steep sided, sharp peaked ridge.

properties.name: Steps
properties.description: An offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Stern Reef
properties.description: An inshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Sponge Pinnacle
properties.description: This is at the east end of Sponge Garden.

properties.name: Dusky Pinnacles - Coral Pinnacle
properties.description: Dusky Pinnacles, with Coral Pinnacle and Sponge Garden lie to the north west of the exposed rocks of Stonehenge North.

properties.name: Stonehenge North
properties.description: A relatively shallow and kelpy area, marked by the exposed rocks to the north of the area.

properties.name: A360 Pinnacle
properties.description: The A360 Pinnacles are a pair of roughly parallel ridges to the southwest of Stonehenge Central, at the edge of the 24 m contour, with a 27 m gully between them.

properties.name: Stonehenge Central
properties.description: Stonehenge Central is relatively shallow and heavily grown with kelp.

properties.name: Stonehenge South
properties.description: A large, flattish, half-tide rock, with a large number of sandy anemones.

properties.name: Stonehenge Blinder
properties.description: A large boulder or outcrop, rising from about 24 m to the south to about 3 m on top, where the surge can be very strong.

properties.name: Strawberry Rocks
properties.description: This is a pleasantly scenic site and there are usually several Cape fur seals to be seen, as well as colourful reef invertebrates.

properties.name: Sunfish Pinnacle
properties.description: A fairly large pinnacle on a rocky bottom on the way to Duiker Point from Hout Bay harbour, which has been picked up quite frequently on the echo sounders of dive boats passing over it.

properties.name: Sunny Cove
properties.description: The access is relatively easy and the site is fairly sheltered from south west swell.

properties.name: Super Fan Reef
properties.description: This site is moderately deep, but shallow enough for a fairly long dive on nitrox.

properties.name: SURG Pinnacles
properties.description: This site is a fairly compact group of large pinnacles which is deeper than most of the nearby dive sites, while still shallow enough for recreational divers.

properties.name: Brittlestar Pinnacle
properties.description: This site is not well explored, and is used mostly by divers who want a dive in the 40 to 50 m depth range which can be ended in shallower water.

properties.name: Coral Crag
properties.description: This site is not well explored, and is used mostly by divers who want a dive in the 40 to 50 m depth range which can be ended in shallower water.

properties.name: Mac's Mark
properties.description: An alternative drop point for a 50 m dive.

properties.name: Tafelberg Deep Pinnacle
properties.description: A huge outcrop of granite with a cluster of pinnacles.

properties.name: Wilhelm's Mark
properties.description: The sand edge runs roughly east-west for about 200 m and is very close to the 50 m contour.

properties.name: Cowrie caves
properties.description: Cowrie Caves is a cluster of boulder pinnacles in the northern part of Tafelberg Reef.

properties.name: Tafelberg Reef North
properties.description: Granite reef of moderately high relief.

properties.name: Tafelberg Reef West
properties.description: Rugged granite outcrop with high relief and sand bottom at about 29 m to the West.

properties.name: Target Reef
properties.description: An offshore rocky reef with concrete structure.

properties.name: Three Anchor Bay
properties.description: A shoreline rocky reef.

properties.name: SS Thomas T. Tucker
properties.description: The "SS Thomas T. Tucker" (Hull Number 269) was a welded steel U.S. liberty ship produced by the Houston Shipbuilding Corporation in 1942.

properties.name: Tivoli Pinnacles
properties.description: This site is part of the Roman Rock reef complex, and is convenient for launches from Simon's Town.

properties.name: Tony's Reef
properties.description: A shoreline rocky reef.

properties.name: Torch Reef
properties.description: A small offshore rocky outcrop.

properties.name: SAS Transvaal
properties.description: A recent wreck.

properties.name: MV Treasure
properties.description: This is a relatively recent wreck of a huge vessel.

properties.name: Tristania
properties.description: The Tristania was built as a motor trawler minesweeper for the Royal Navy in 1940 in Selby, West Yorkshire.

properties.name: Troglodyte's Cove
properties.description: A shoreline rocky reef.

properties.name: T.S. McEwan (Smoky Sue)
properties.description: The steam tug T.S. McEwan was well known in Table Bay harbour for many years.

properties.name: Twin Towers
properties.description: An offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Two Oceans Aquarium
properties.description: The aquarium provides the opportunity for diving in a controlled environment where you are guaranteed to see a large number of a variety of large fish.

properties.name: SS Umhlali
properties.description: The SS Umhlali was a British registered steel cargo and passenger ship of 3380 gross registered tons, built at the Laing yard in Deptford in 1904.

properties.name: Vogelsteen
properties.description: Notable for the beds of pebbles, silt, and shells between the rocky inshore zone and the flat sand bottom further offshore, where large numbers of the False Bay burrowing anemone (Cerianthid) can be found.

properties.name: Vulcan Rock
properties.description: The exposed rock is the top of a very big granite tor.

properties.name: North Ridge Pinnacle
properties.description: To the north of the exposed rock is a long ridge running northwest to southeast, with a cluster of pinnacles a short distance to the northeast, with the shallowest pinnacle rising to within about 3 m of the surface.

properties.name: West Ridge Pinnacle
properties.description: An offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Rocksucker Ridge West Pinnacle
properties.description: A fairly large cluster of huge boulders about 55 m long from east to west and 30 m wide north to south at 15 m, rising to flattish tops at around 11 to 15 m, riven by huge cracks extending to below 24 m in places.

properties.name: Rocksucker Ridge East Pinnacle
properties.description: The east end of the ridge, and probably the high point.

properties.name: Western Deep
properties.description: A small area of reef to the west of Whittle Rock reef, probably the deepest of the Off-Whittle western reefs.

properties.name: Whale Rock
properties.description: An offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Whirlpool Cove
properties.description: A shoreline rocky reef.

properties.name: Aoife's Reef
properties.description: An extensive offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Bruce's Reef
properties.description: Bruce's Reef, also known as Stingray central or Stingray HQ, is an area of reef just inside the MPA first dived in 2020.

properties.name: Bus-stop (the Gnarly wall)
properties.description: Bus-stop overhang is a feature on the Gnarly Wall, which is the north face of the east outcrop of Tower Ridge.

properties.name: Butt Rocks
properties.description: A small area of high reef about 100 m to the west of Western Reef Pinnacles, across a narrow sand tongue at about 32 m.

properties.name: Caves Complex
properties.description: An extensive offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Criss-cross Cracks
properties.description: The Criss-cross Cracks area is a high flattish topped area at the south of the East Ridge, with the shallow point at about 21 m split by several relatively narrow and moderately deep cracks.

properties.name: Deep South Pinnacles
properties.description: An extensive offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: East Ridge North Pinnacle
properties.description: East Ridge North Pinnacle, also known as "The Knuckles", is a massive outcrop about 63 m long northwest to southeast, and 45 m wide at 27 m depth.

properties.name: Far Southwest Pinnacle
properties.description: A bit south of the Western Reef Pinnacle.

properties.name: Flash Pinnacle
properties.description: A tall tapering granite pinnacle with a triangular section and small flattish top at about 16 m.

properties.name: Fractal Zones
properties.description: The far northwest and western side of the reef has a large area of interlocking low reef and sand areas.

properties.name: Georgina's anchor
properties.description: A large iron anchor on the boulders at the base of the south slopes of the southeastern pinnacle, of unknown provenance, at a depth of 29 m, at S34°14.935' E18°33.784'.

properties.name: Grant's Spike
properties.description: The tallest of these pinnacles has been named Grant's Spike.

properties.name: Grant's Wall
properties.description: An extensive offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Gullies
properties.description: An extensive offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Labyrinth
properties.description: An extensive offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Labyrinth South Pinnacle
properties.description: South of the Labyrinth there is a large area within the 27 m contour called the Sponge Gardens, for the number and variety of colourful sponges near that depth.

properties.name: Mossie's Cave and pinnacle
properties.description: The position of one deep overhang or cave has been marked at S34°14.972' E18°33.420' as Mossie's Cave.

properties.name: M&M Tower (the Spark plug)
properties.description: The central pinnacle and shallowest point on Tower Ridge, a section of reef parallel to, and to the southwest of, Whaleback ridge.

properties.name: Northwest Corner Pinnacles
properties.description: An extensive offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Northwest Passage
properties.description: Right at the northwestern tip of the Whittle Rock reefs.

properties.name: Northwest Pinnacle
properties.description: There is a small, fairly steep and very localised pinnacle area on a generally lower profile area of massive bedrock of the Northwest Rise.

properties.name: Peter's Ridge
properties.description: An extensive offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Shards Cluster
properties.description: There is a cluster of huge angular boulders known as "The Shards" at the northeasternmost extent of the main reef, off the Euphrates Rise, projecting beyond the general line of the perimeter into the surrounding sand.

properties.name: Southeast Pinnacle
properties.description: An extensive offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Table Top Pinnacle
properties.description: East and a bit south from the Caves Complex, Table Top pinnacle is a massive outcrop with a fairly flat top about 20 m in diameter at about 14.5 to 15 m depth.

properties.name: Ultima Thule
properties.description: This is the farthest northwest reef that is still considered part of Whittle Rock reef.

properties.name: West Pinnacle
properties.description: About 50 m due west of the main pinnacle, and at 7 m, the second shallowest point of the reef.

properties.name: Western Reef Pinnacle
properties.description: An area of moderate profile reef to the west of the previously surveyed areas, marked by a shallower area at 19 m depth on top, and local bottom at a bit below 27 m on sand to the north and west.

properties.name: Whaleback Pinnacles
properties.description: Whaleback Pinnacles is a group of pinnacles at the northwest end of Whaleback Ridge, with a small sand patch at about 25 m depth off the northeast end of the ridge, and another at about 27 m to the southwest.

properties.name: Whaleback Rock
properties.description: Whaleback Rock is at the southeastern end of Whaleback Ridge.

properties.name: Whittle Rock
properties.description: The main reef near the 5 m pinnacle is the shallowest part of the reef, with an extensive area above 15 m, and several parts above 12 m, separated by gaps and gullies of varying depth and width.

properties.name: Wreckless Rock and the Little Labyrinth
properties.description: An extensive offshore rocky reef.

properties.name: Wilhelm's Wall
properties.description: This is a very pretty reef, and the top of the reef is deep enough not to break in conditions that are diveable.

properties.name: Windmill Beach
properties.description: This site has very easy and protected beach entry and a small cove with sandy bottom that is suitable for training exercises, while also having a varied topography, diverse ecology and large area.

properties.name: Dangerous Doug Reef
properties.description: Medium profile granite reef with occasional areas of higher and lower profile.

properties.name: Lace Reef
properties.description: The highest point of the reef is at about 23 m.

properties.name: Outer Windmill
properties.description: Sand bottom is at about 12 m, and top of the reef at about 6.5 m.

properties.name: Three Bears Pinnacle
properties.description: Three Bears Pinnacle has three outcrops; one large, one small, and one in between in a tight little clump, and is named for the children's story.

properties.name: Windmill Offshore
properties.description: Granite outcrop with deep sandy bottomed gullies and indentations and a few high points.

properties.name: Windtoy Reef
properties.description: This part of the reef comprises a relatively small area of high profile outcrops and large boulders in the northern part of the reef, surrounded by lower profile reef and relatively small boulders and rubble.

properties.name: Windtoy Reef South
properties.description: Relatively open, but fairly high profile reef.

properties.name: MV Winton
properties.description: A shallow wreck site on a sand bottom, within swimming distance of the beach.

properties.name: Wreckless Ridge
properties.description: First dived in 2021 by Wreckless Divers.

properties.name: York Shoal
properties.description: York shoal is very seldom dived by recreational divers, because it is fairly far from the launch sites, near a known feeding area for great white sharks, and is virtually unknown to the diving public.

properties.name: Zigzag Reef
properties.description: This is one of the deeper reef sites within a short distance from the popular False Bay launching areas.
